questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The metropolitan city and japanese culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing being on exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. When I finally arrived at Waseda, Tokyo there was a lot of helpful information. The hold approval proces before going was definitely the hardest part.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help finding accomodation and meeting other people on exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was a bit hard to figure out what courses i was able to take. And some of the courses where supposed to be in english but then changed last minutes.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to get a spot at the international student dorm

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There where a kithcen at the dorm, but I also had a lot of my meals at resturants/street food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Its super freindly and convinient. When you are on exhange there is a lot of things going on and the fact that the dorm was so used to exchange student and knew what it was about made that part easy and safe. Then you were able to use energy elsewhere (school, freinds, culture etc)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There was a big data set with couses and then i looked them all through one by one. What topics, which day, teaching language, level etc. It was very hard to get a hole overview of possibilities and some of the courses that i wanted to choose, that i found before going, was not open to excjange students or teached in english. 

Then I was able to take some courses from other faculties which was nice. So in the end it turned out well, but it was kind of frustration and "lonely" proces because you do it all before you really know anyone.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Assistens at campus

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not really succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to get a overview of youre possibilities before going. Choose some courses and then enjoy. Eventhough I did not have my dream academic courses I learned a lot of useful stuff about culture and life.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a easier than UCPH at master level. But the workload in terms of paper where higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar teaching but way more digital interaction - had to turn papers in every week for 6 courses, not just going to an exam in the end of the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: - agriculture economics, history of japanese media and politics, comparative politics of new democracies, international political economy, digital sustainability, japanese language course.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: digital sustainability

What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None - there where a lot of difference, but i dont think it was challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The respect towards what you do - no matters if it is in the supermarket, in the train, going to school, being with to other people. There is no kaos in Tokyo eventhough it is a chaotic setup. It so safe and clean and well functioning.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Its a big experience and it can feel overwhelming when you are in the middle of it for sure. But just try to enjoy as much as possible. Go take a change, go on a weekend trip with freinds you just let life happens. Before you know it, you will be home again. 
- Engage in student activities in the beginning and try to get freinds quickly 
- Try to apply for scholarships way ahead of youre stay. It is expencive to be on exhange

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go go go!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Freinds, cultural knowhow, and personal learning. The best personal "lesson" was the proud feeling I got towards myself, when I realized that im actually living in Tokyo/on the other side of the world, having a good time with school, freinds and daily life. And that I made it all happen by myself (with university help ofc). But all the effort and applying show was so much worth it ind the end. 

And then the "active" way of interacting with people in a new country. You have to built up and use youre network so much more than when you are in your routines back home. 

And the experience was for sure an eyeopener towards new exchange experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The weeks before school really started. I was super nervouse about everything and it felt lonely being on your own i japan. The semester is 3 months behind from DK, so the "waiting" time was challenging. As soon as the semester started your are busy with everything going on an do not have time to think so much.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
